text.content: Across four sprints you produced a set of deliverables that build on each other — the architecture decision brief that names the pattern, the multi-agent design diagram that shows how the agents relate, the memory and state specification that describes what the system knows and what it forgets, and the redesigned canvas with the test record that proves it behaves the way the specification says. The teaching canvas came away in Sprint 4. What you submit is your own architecture on your own domain.

text.content: Sprint 1: Architecture decision. The one-page architecture decision brief covering the six sections — decision, pattern, inputs and outputs, the three pillars, rejected alternative, and the conditions under which you would revisit the decision.

text.content: Sprint 2: Multi-agent design. The design diagram with every agent named, information flow shown, routing decision points marked, information boundaries called out, and at least one fallback path — plus the written design rationale covering diagnosis and justification, agent roles, the information boundary, and the fallback strategy.

rich_text.plain_text: Sprint 2: Multi-agent design. The design diagram with every agent named, information flow shown, routing decision points marked, information boundaries called out, and at least one fallback path — plus the written design rationale covering diagnosis and justification, agent roles, the information boundary, and the fallback strategy.

text.content: Sprint 3: Memory and state architecture. The four-section specification: the memory boundary map with persistence scope, what must not persist and how each item is prevented, the state recovery design naming the failure scenario and the safe state, and the failure isolation assessment of which agents may write to which state keys.

rich_text.plain_text: Sprint 3: Memory and state architecture. The four-section specification: the memory boundary map with persistence scope, what must not persist and how each item is prevented, the state recovery design naming the failure scenario and the safe state, and the failure isolation assessment of which agents may write to which state keys.

text.content: Sprint 4: Integration and testing. The redesign in four stages — archetype staged on the canvas, memory boundaries enforced, state handoff and recovery wired, and the five safeguards confirmed. Then the nine tests in three groups: baseline function, boundary conditions, and architecture-specific validation. Refine until each safeguard holds under the test it was designed for, and export the canvas.

text.content: The module project moves from a set of design documents and a canvas into something you can stand behind and explain. The architecture brief named a pattern, the diagram showed the relationships, the specification drew the boundaries, and the testing work turned all of it from a claim into evidence.
